evidence: Receiving DO2 drops ~6 mg/L abruptly between 50.0h (11.009) and 50.2h (5.279), continuing to 4.510 mg/L at 52.0h
Source batches (source-1/2/3) show DO2 ~10.5-11 mg/L during hours 50-52, so the receiving anomaly is site-specific
P assay at 48h: 3.010 g/L, matching source trajectory; deficit is oxygen transfer vs demand, not low productivity yet
Forward model keep: min DO 1.458 mg/L, 4.6 h below limit, infeasible; increase_air: min DO 1.65, still infeasible; combined: min DO 1.82, infeasible
Forward model strong_feed_reduction: min DO 2.96 mg/L, 0 h below limit, product mass 272.6 kg, post-decision feasible, 4/5 sensitivity members feasible
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 broke from ~11 mg/L to ~4.5-5 mg/L between t=50h and t=52h, unlike matched source batches (~10.5 mg/L at the same phase), indicating a large OUR increase that the current aeration/feed regime cannot sustain. KEEP and mild corrections (reduce_feed, increase_air, combined) all predict post-decision DO below the 2 mg/L minimum oxygen constraint in the source-calibrated forward model (minimum DO 1.46-1.82 mg/L with multiple below-limit hours), i.e., oxygen-constraint violations. Strong feed reduction (feed x0.6 with air x1.15) is the only bounded action predicted fully feasible: minimum DO 2.96 mg/L, zero below-limit hours, and the highest retained product mass (~273 kg vs ~206-243 kg for alternatives), with the best sensitivity robustness (4/5 members feasible). Stop is rejected because it yields zero counted production. The physics model is an imperfect source-calibrated prediction, but the direction of the evidence (falling DO toward the 2 mg/L floor) strongly favors the strongest feed cut.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and the receiving process may differ in hidden parameters; DO2 values are noisy (±0.5 mg/L). If the DO drop were a sensor artifact rather than real OUR surge, strong feed reduction would over-restrict feeding, though the sensitivity range (206-622 kg product mass) suggests it still preserves more product mass than violating the oxygen limit. The 1.2 mg/L observed drop in 2 hours suggests the DO could breach 2 mg/L within ~4-5 hours under KEEP, so waiting for an extra assay (4 h turnaround) would risk operating below the minimum DO; hence intervening now.
